description:
Offline demonstration digital twin of ORNL's Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE, 1965-69) built on the OUTRAM PARK suite. Scope per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md: OFFLINE DEMONSTRATION / V&V / education only — no operational or live-plant coupling; MSRE is a public, decommissioned benchmark (ORNL-TM / ORNL-4xxx report series), so 'real time' means a real-time-capable simulation loop replaying/assimilating the historical record, not hardware monitoring. Data-policy clean (all MSRE data open literature).

Architecture: two-tier. OFFLINE high-fidelity (MC k-eig + depletion via outram-mc-libs+njoy; CFD via outram-foam; molten-salt Gibbs FP thermochemistry) generates reduced-order tables/models. REAL-TIME tier runs a circulating-fuel point-kinetics + 1-D loop TH (tuas/tampines, which already has FLiBe + HITEC salt correlations) + lumped Xe/FP-migration model in outram-park-digital-twin-engine (egui), with a state estimator (chem-eng real-time scaffolding) assimilating replayed MSRE data — which doubles as validation.

MSRE-specific hard physics: (1) circulating fuel => delayed-neutron precursors advect out of core (flow-dependent reactivity) - the defining effect; (2) Xe-135 gas stripping; (3) FP migration into three destinations (noble gases->off-gas, noble metals->plate on graphite/Hastelloy-N, salt-seekers->dissolved/precipitate) governed by salt redox (UF3/UF4).

Phasing: P0 zero-power circulating-fuel kinetics -> P1 add TH feedback -> P2 Xe+depletion -> P3 FP migration+chemistry -> P4 data assimilation. Each phase validates against a published MSRE dataset. All AI-assisted output is untrusted draft pending human V&V.

description:
External blocker for op-9vo6.11 (GitHub issue #35 step 11, 'Integrate reusable kopitiam-pdf reader'). Upstream work is kopitiam#96 ('kopitiam pdf refactor for kovan'), which per its latest comment is functionally complete: all 12 phases landed (68145b9), kpdf.rs went 3899 -> 630 lines, the reusable pieces sit behind an egui feature separate from the kpdf standalone-shell feature (cargo tree verified zero eframe/rfd in an egui-only build), and there is a third-party embedding example (examples/embed_reader.rs) built by CI.

IT IS NOT PUBLISHED. Verified against the crates.io index 2026-08-31: latest kopitiam-pdf is 0.3.1, whose feature table is

    default = ["kpdf"]
    kpdf    = ["dep:eframe", "dep:egui", "dep:rfd"]

There is no separate 'egui' feature in ANY published version, so the reader extraction is unavailable to this workspace. crates/kovan/Cargo.toml:107 pins 0.3.1 (set by commit 5e504e3f, 'moved kovan to use v0.3.1 of kopitiam pdf').

NOTHING TO DO HERE FROM THIS WORKSPACE. Per CLAUDE.md's hard boundary, this workspace CONSUMES kopitiam binaries/releases only -- never a path or git dependency on a working copy, never a local patched build, never an edit or PR out of this tree. The deliverable is the upstream publish; this bead exists so op-9vo6.11 has a real blocker edge rather than a note buried in a description. Close it when a version carrying the separate egui feature is on crates.io, recording the version and the date.
title: kopitiam-pdf: publish 0.3.2+ with the reusable reader behind a separate egui feature (blocks kovan redesign step 11)

description: Incremental (or QuickHull) 3D convex hull producing a closed triangle Mesh from a set of Vec3 points. Reuse the existing robust boolean_predicates::orient3d for the orientation/visibility tests. Handle degeneracies (duplicate/coplanar points). Complements the CSG/boolean suite (bounding volumes, convex decomposition input).
title: outram-blender: 3D convex hull from a point set

description: Add STL read/write, the lingua franca for surface meshes and the standard DAGMC/Monte-Carlo feed. Export: fan-triangulate faces, per-facet normal, ASCII (to_stl_ascii) + binary (to_stl_binary) + disk writers. Import: parse ASCII/binary triangle soup into a Mesh (from_stl_ascii/from_stl_binary/from_stl_bytes with size-heuristic auto-detect); STL has no shared vertices so import returns the raw soup for the caller to weld() into topology. New stl module (I/O, not a MeshOp). V&V: cube -> to_stl_ascii/binary -> from_stl -> weld -> V8 E18 F12 chi2; binary size = 84 + 50*ntri; round-trip vertex positions preserved to f32 precision.
title: outram-blender: STL import/export (ASCII + binary)

description: Found 2026-08-11 by correlation audit during op-4542. crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/parallel_heat_exchangers.rs:121-145. The equal-temperature early return computes U*A*(T_amb - T_fluid) (heat INTO fluid, matching the doc); the LMTD branch passes ambient as the cold pair and fluid as the hot pair, yielding T_fluid - T_amb (heat OUT of fluid) -- opposite sign convention between the two branches. Inline comment at L133-134 claims delta T = ambient - fluid, contradicting the actual argument order. Additionally log_mean_temperature_difference panics when hot < cold, so the function panics outright whenever ambient is hotter than the fluid -- the very heat-input case its doc describes.
title: tuas: LMTD ambient heat-flux helper has opposite sign conventions and panics when ambient hotter than fluid

description: outram-mc-libs' Tally struct holds filters: Vec<Box<dyn Filter>>, which violates BOTH the workspace no-trait-objects rule and the no-Box rule, and it forces the violation onto consumers: outram-blender's sim::cell_flux_tally (src/sim.rs:304) has to construct Box<dyn Filter> to use it. The filter set is closed and known at compile time, so per the workspace Rust design rules it should be an enum (FilterKind) with exhaustive match dispatch. Fix belongs in outram-mc-libs; outram-blender's call site then simplifies. Found during the 2026-08-07 outram-blender bookkeeping pass.
title: outram-mc-libs: Tally filters use Vec<Box<dyn Filter>> — enum-dispatch them
